items.statement: Do not rely on a balance's built-in auto-calibration feature alone; also perform external performance checks of the balance.
items.quote: The auto-calibration feature of a balance may not be relied upon to the exclusion of an external performance check

items.statement: For scales with a built-in auto-calibrator, perform external performance checks periodically; these may be less frequent than for scales without this feature.
items.quote: For a scale with a built-in auto-calibrator, we recommend that external performance checks be performed on a periodic basis, but less frequently as compared to a scale without this feature.

items.statement: Set the frequency of balance performance checks based on how often the scale is used and on the criticality and tolerance of the process or analytical step.
items.quote: The frequency of performance checks depends on the frequency of use of the scale and the criticality and tolerance of the process or analytical step.

items.statement: Periodically verify the calibration of a balance's auto-calibrator (commonly once a year) using NIST-traceable standards or NIST-accredited standards used in other countries.
items.quote: Additionally, the calibration of an auto-calibrator should be periodically verified—a common frequency is once a year—using National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-traceable standards or NIST-accredited standards in use in other countries.

items.statement: Forced degradation (stress testing) of the drug product may be omitted when the degradation routes and the suitability of the analytical procedures can be determined using: stress testing data on the drug substance; reference materials for process impurities and degradants; accelerated and long-term study data on the drug substance; and accelerated and long-term study data on the drug product.
items.quote: Drug product stress testing (forced degradation) may not be necessary when the routes of degradation and the suitability of the analytical procedures can be determined through use of the following:
items.condition: degradation routes and method suitability can be determined from listed data

items.statement: Establish and document the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and reproducibility of test methods.
items.quote: Section 211.165(e) of the CGMP regulations states that the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility of test methods shall be established and documented

items.statement: Use stability test methods that are reliable, meaningful and specific, so that the active ingredient content, degradation products and other components of interest can be measured accurately without interference (stability indicating).
items.quote: Further, 21 CFR 211.166(a)(3) requires that stability test methods be reliable, meaningful, and specific, which means that the content of the active ingredient, degradation products, and other components of interest in a drug product can be accurately measured without interference, often called stability indicating.

items.statement: Where needed to ensure stability test methods are stability indicating, evaluate test method specificity in forced degradation studies of both the drug substance and the drug product (for example, exposure to extremes of pH, temperature, oxygen).
items.quote: However, evaluating the specificity of the test methods during forced degradation studies (i.e., exposing the drug to extremes of pH, temperature, oxygen, etc.) of the drug substance and drug product often is necessary to ensure that stability test methods are stability indicating.

items.statement: In certain circumstances, a forced degradation study of only the drug substance may be enough to evaluate whether a test method is stability indicating.
items.quote: But in certain circumstances, conducting a forced degradation study of just the drug substance may be sufficient to evaluate the stability-indicating properties of a test method.

items.statement: When deciding whether forced degradation studies of the drug product are needed, evaluate whether the test method can assay the drug substance, degradants and impurities in the presence of each other without interference.
items.quote: Generally, in determining whether it is necessary to conduct forced degradation studies of the drug product, the specificity of the test method should be evaluated for its ability to assay drug substance, degradants, and impurities, in the presence of each other, without interference.
items.condition: deciding on drug product forced degradation

items.statement: Ensure that evaluation also gives assurance that no interaction can occur between drug substance, degradants, impurities, excipients and the container-closure system over the shelf life of the finished product.
items.quote: The evaluation also should provide assurance that there is not a potential for interaction between the drug substance, degradants, impurities, excipients, and container-closure system during the course of the shelf life of the finished drug product.

items.statement: Fully document the rationale for decisions on the extent of forced degradation studies and the rationale for concluding that a test method is stability indicating.
items.quote: Last, the rationale for any decision made concerning the extent of the forced degradation studies conducted as well as the rationale for concluding that a test method is stability indicating should be fully documented.

items.statement: When testing large volume parenterals for subvisible particulate matter, do not average results across the units tested in a batch or lot to decide whether the batch meets specification.
items.quote: It is not acceptable to take the average among the LVP units tested in each batch/lot when following this method because the purpose of this method is to measure and limit intra-batch variability.

items.statement: Test particulate matter samples first by light obscuration; if a sample fails the specified limits, the microscopic assay may then be used.
items.quote: Normally, samples are first tested by the light obscuration method; if the sample fails the specified limits, the microscopic assay method can then be used.

items.statement: The microscopic method may be used as the only particulate test if there is a documented technical reason or product interference that makes light obscuration unsuitable or its results invalid.
items.quote: However, the microscopic method can be the sole test if there is a documented technical reason or interference from the product under test that would make the light obscuration method unsuitable or the results invalid.

items.statement: For the light obscuration particulate count, use at least 2 aliquots of 5 mL from each sampled unit or from the pooled sample, and average the aliquot results for comparison with the specification.
items.quote: At least 2, 5-mL aliquots from each sampled unit or the pooled sample (see below) are to be used in the particulate count determination, and the results from these aliquots are to be averaged for comparison with the specification.

items.statement: In light obscuration testing, discard the results of the first aliquot examined and retain the subsequent aliquots (2 or more).
items.quote: (The results of the first aliquot examined by light obscuration are to be discarded, and the subsequent aliquots—2 or more—are retained.)

items.statement: Pool units before particulate analysis only if each unit holds less than 25 mL; in that case 10 or more units may be pooled.
items.quote: Pooling units prior to analysis is permitted only if the volume in each unit is less than 25 mL, in which case 10 or more units may be pooled.

items.statement: Where small or large volume parenteral units hold 25 mL or more each, examine single units by the particulate test.
items.quote: If the volume in the SVP or LVP is 25 mL or more per unit, single units are to be examined by this method

items.statement: For parenteral units of 25 mL or more, base the number of units tested for particulate matter on a statistically sound sampling plan that considers product volume, historical particle numbers relative to limits, particle size distribution and unit-to-unit variability of particle counts.
items.quote: As to the number of individual units to be tested for LVP and SVP units having a volume of 25mL or more, the USP states that the number of units tested depends on "statistically sound sampling plans," and "sampling plans should be based on consideration of product volume, numbers of particles historically found to be present in comparison to limits, particle size distribution of particles present, and variability of particle counts between units."

items.statement: With proper justification, fewer than 10 units in total may be tested per batch for particulate matter (for large volume parenterals and pooled small volume parenterals).
items.quote: The USP also suggests that the total number of units tested for any given batch may be less than 10 units (for LVP and pooled SVPs) with proper justification.

items.statement: TOC or TC may be used to monitor cleaning residues routinely and for cleaning validation.
items.quote: We think TOC or TC can be an acceptable method for monitoring residues routinely and for cleaning validation.

items.statement: Before using TOC for residues, establish that a substantial amount of the contaminating material is organic and contains carbon that oxidizes under the TOC test conditions.
items.quote: But in order for TOC to be functionally suitable, it should first be established that a substantial amount of the contaminating material(s) is organic and contains carbon that can be oxidized under TOC test conditions.

items.statement: TOC may be justified for both direct surface sampling and indirect (rinse water) sampling.
items.quote: TOC use may be justified for direct surface sample testing as well as indirect (rinse water) sample testing.

items.statement: When using TOC, attribute all detected carbon to the target compound(s) when comparing with the established limit.
items.quote: In either case, because TOC does not identify or distinguish among different compounds containing oxidizable carbon, any detected carbon is to be attributed to the target compound(s) for comparing with the established limit.

items.statement: Limit background carbon (carbon from sources other than the contaminant being removed) as much as possible when using TOC.
items.quote: Thus, a firm should limit background carbon (i.e., carbon from sources other than the contaminant being removed) as much as possible.

items.statement: Correct the established TOC limit, or the detected residue amount compared with the specification, for the carbon content of the target material.
items.quote: The established limit, or the amount of residue detected for comparison to the specification, should correct for the target material's composition of carbon.

items.statement: Perform recovery studies for the cleaning residue test method, including TOC.
items.quote: As for any cleaning method, recovery studies are necessary (21 CFR 211.160(b)).

items.statement: If TOC samples are held for long periods before analysis, verify the effect of the holding time on accuracy and limit of quantitation.
items.quote: If TOC samples are being held for long periods of time before analysis, a firm should verify the impact of sample holding time on accuracy and limit of quantitation.

items.quote: Also, alternative methods may be needed to test high-pressure cylinders for cleaning solution residues.

items.statement: Use validated methods for routine testing of raw materials, in-process materials and finished products when manufacturing finished drug products.
items.quote: The CGMP regulations require the use of validated methods when performing routine testing of raw material, in-process material, and finished products (21 CFR 211.160, 211.165(e), and 211.194) for manufacturing finished drug products.

items.statement: Test methods based on scientifically sound principles (e.g. sufficient accuracy and precision) that are not fully validated may be used in certain instances during an investigation of a potential quality problem or defect.
items.quote: FDA recognizes, however, that test methods developed based on scientifically sound principles (e.g., sufficient accuracy and precision) but that are not fully validated may be suitable for use in certain instances during an investigation of a potential quality problem or defect.
items.condition: during an investigation of a potential quality problem

items.statement: When testing components or products with an unvalidated method, recognize that the results may carry greater uncertainty than results from validated methods.
items.quote: When a company, for whatever reason, tests drug components or products using an unvalidated method, it is important to recognize the possibility of greater uncertainty in the test results derived from these unvalidated test methods, as compared to validated test methods.

items.statement: Review all test results on drug components or products obtained with unvalidated methods to assess the need for follow-up action.
items.quote: Accordingly, we expect all such test results on drug components or products to be reviewed to assess the need for follow-up action

items.statement: Non-penicillin finished drug products may be marketed if they are tested by the codified method and found not to be contaminated with penicillin.
items.quote: 21 CFR 211.176, Penicillin Contamination, allows marketing of non-penicillin finished drug products if they are tested using the codified method and found not to be contaminated with penicillin.

items.statement: Do not release a non-penicillin product tested for penicillin unless all other applicable CGMP requirements have also been met.
items.quote: However, it is not acceptable to release the product unless all other applicable CGMP requirements have been met.

items.statement: Perform manufacturing operations for penicillin drug products in facilities separate from those used for non-penicillin human drug products.
items.quote: Notably, 21 CFR 211.42(d) requires that manufacturing operations for penicillin drug products be performed in facilities separate from those used for non-penicillin human drug products.

items.statement: Keep air-handling systems for penicillin and non-penicillin drug products completely separate.
items.quote: Similarly, 21 CFR 211.46(d) requires that air-handling systems for penicillin and non-penicillin drug products be completely separate.

items.statement: Do not rely on testing alone to make compliant a non-penicillin product made in a facility sharing equipment or an air-handling system with a penicillin production area.
items.quote: For example, if a non-penicillin product is made in a facility that shares equipment or an air-handling system with a penicillin production area (in violation of § 211.46(d)), the non-penicillin product cannot be made CGMP-compliant through testing alone.
items.condition: facility shares equipment or air handling with penicillin area

items.statement: Where other separate production areas were possibly exposed to penicillin by accident (such as a door left open to a penicillin-dedicated area), testing the products from those areas for penicillin may justify their release.
items.quote: However, if a door is accidentally left open between a penicillin-dedicated area and other separate production areas, resulting in possible exposure of the other areas to penicillin, testing those other products for penicillin could justify their release for distribution.
items.condition: accidental possible exposure of separate areas

items.statement: Ensure all sampling plans and acceptance criteria used to test and release non-penicillin products, including any penicillin contamination testing, are adequate to ensure the product meets all its specifications.
items.quote: However, as per 21 CFR 211.165, all sampling plans and acceptance criteria used for testing and release of the non-penicillin product, including any testing for penicillin contamination, must be adequate to ensure the tested product meets all of its specifications.
